intents.text: edit code over ssh: syntax highlighting, multiple buffers, no X11 and no clipboard integration
build small C projects locally with make
reach the machine over ssh with key auth only, no password auth, no X forwarding

never block the terminal on a long build: a terminal multiplexer that starts split into two panes, so a compile can run in one while I keep working in the other. Scriptable session and pane control from the shell. No mouse, no clipboard, no X.
serve this machine's ebuild tree and binary packages to other AIos nodes over HTTP, and take code updates from a peer the same way
rebuild the same package repeatedly without recompiling what did not change: a compiler cache sized for a few full package builds, shared across every build on this machine

when this machine is compiling something large and other machines on the network are offering spare capacity, hand them the individual compile jobs instead of doing all of them here; when nobody is offering, compile everything locally without treating that as a failure
work in the cockpit's shell as the named operator account rather than root, with passwordless escalation to root for administration; the agent session itself stays root

make_conf.why: intent[4]: this node serves its binary packages to peers; zstd keeps the binhost seed small and fast to unpack. Carried over from the reviewed lock, which the re-lowering dropped without naming a reason.
intent[5]: normalizes per-build paths so repeated rebuilds of the same package hit the cache
intent[5]: one cache location shared across every build on this machine
intent[5]: sized for a few full package builds
intent[4]: fixed location for the binary packages nginx exports over HTTP
intent[0]/intent[3]: no X11, no clipboard, no graphical session anywhere; intent[2]: no password auth path; target init is dinit

notes: DISTCC_HOSTS and PORTAGE_BINHOST are refused per policy: intent[6] is served by sys-devel/distcc with zeroconf discovery, and intent[4] by nginx + PKGDIR. The peer/binhost addresses are per-build environment, not machine state.

FEATURES (ccache, distcc) and MAKEOPTS are owned by the spec, so intent[5]/intent[6] activation flags are not emitted here; without FEATURES="ccache distcc" set by the spec these packages are installed but inert.
intent[1], intent[2], intent[4] have no probes: dev-build/make, net-misc/openssh, www-servers/nginx and dev-vcs/git can never be minimized away.
Key-only ssh and disabled X forwarding are sshd_config runtime settings; USE=-pam is the only build-time part expressible here.
tmux starting split into two panes is a tmux.conf/session-script matter, not a build decision.
Serving the ebuild tree over HTTP additionally needs nginx's autoindex http module enabled via NGINX_MODULES_HTTP; that variable is not part of this schema.
All listed packages build on musl/aarch64; none are known to be glibc-only. distcc's zeroconf support pulls net-dns/avahi, which is musl-compatible.

spec_digest re-stamped by hand for the [agent] provider change (anthropic -> fallback) without re-running the lowering. Which backend is ASKED NEXT time is not an input to any decision recorded here: the packages, USE flags and make.conf below were produced by claude-opus-5 and are unchanged, and generated_by still names it. Re-lowering to pick up a provider rename would have churned every USE decision for nothing, which is the opposite of a reviewable diff.

app-admin/sudo added by hand for intent[7], with the spec_digest re-stamped, rather than by a re-lowering: lowering is nondeterministic and a full re-run churns every reviewed USE decision to add one package (this file already records one such overruling). The flags here match the binary the live node built and cached (sudo-1.9.17_p2 emerged with USE=-sendmail, global -pam), so boot-time restore reuses that binpkg instead of rebuilding.

use.why: intent[7]: escalation is passwordless by policy and this machine has no PAM stack anywhere (global USE -pam, init is dinit); sudo authenticates via NOPASSWD in /etc/sudoers.d/aios-operator, not via a module

intent[7]: sudo's default USE pulls mail-mta/nullmailer + app-admin/metalog + virtual/mta — six packages to email failed-sudo reports on a machine with no mail. Logging to syslog is untouched by this flag.

packages.why: intent[7]: the operator account works in the shell pane and escalates to root with sudo; the account and the sudoers drop-in are boot-time work in aios-init, the binary is this package

intent[6] is served by the mesh, not by mDNS: aios.toml states that WHICH machines compiles go to is topology that never enters the lockfile and comes from `python3 -m aios.mesh distcc` at build time, and MANUAL.md states nothing on this mesh runs distccd at all. zeroconf therefore duplicates existing discovery while pulling 72 extra packages (net-dns/avahi, dbus, glib, gobject-introspection) onto a musl target. A live lowering proposed +zeroconf and was overruled for it, as one was previously overruled on system.features.
